description: Write a page of Markdown (headings, prose, lists, tables) in which every quotation is a reference, and Scriptura inserts the exact text: the model never types the quotation. Put {{Rep. 514a}}, {{John 1:1|grc,kjv}} (editions or languages after "|"), {{plato-republic/21#p-0}} or a scriptura.si link where a quotation goes, on its own line for a block (the original beside the English, with its verdict, citation and permanent link) or inside a sentence for a short inline quotation. Ordinary quotation blocks (> "…" — Plato, Republic) are checked against the texts and shown with the real wording. A reference that is not found shows plainly as "not found". In hosts that render apps it opens as a typeset page the person can expand, copy as Markdown, copy as a bibliography (MLA, Chicago, SBL, BibTeX) or print; in other hosts the result is the Markdown with the quotations filled in, each with its link and citation. Cite the quotations with the links the result lists.
